keyVerseText: And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness. bestow: or, put on
rootMeaning: The word εὐσχημοσύνη (euschēmosýnē) derives from the root εὐσχήμων (euschḗmōn), which conveys a sense of being comely, honorable, and well-formed. This root carries a nuance of decorum and nobility, suggesting not only external beauty but also an inner dignity and propriety. Thus, beyond the simple English gloss of 'comeliness,' the root emphasizes a gracefulness and elegance that reflects honorable character and fitting behavior.
usageInScripture: This term appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in 1 Corinthians 12:23, where it is translated as 'comeliness.' Its singular occurrence highlights a focused usage related to the body metaphor, emphasizing the value and honor given to parts of the body that might otherwise be considered less honorable. The consistent translation as 'comeliness' underscores a theme of inherent grace and decorum that is bestowed abundantly even on those parts deemed uncomely, suggesting a divine revaluation of worth and dignity.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding εὐσχημοσύνη enriches our grasp of the Christian concept of the body and community. It teaches that God honors and dignifies what may appear less attractive or less significant by human standards, reflecting His grace that transcends superficial judgments. This word reminds believers that true honor and beauty in the body of Christ come from God’s gracious bestowal of dignity and decorum. It invites a Christ-centered humility and appreciation for all members of the body, fostering unity and mutual respect grounded in divine grace rather than human esteem.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Corinthians 12:23, Paul states that the parts of the body considered less honorable receive more abundant honor, and that the 'uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness.' The use of εὐσχημοσύνη here highlights that what may seem unattractive or insignificant is endowed with a special grace and elegance by God’s design. This word deepens the verse’s meaning by portraying divine honor as a transformative grace that elevates and dignifies all members of the body, encouraging believers to value every part of the church community.
